decisions.executionNote: Raise right wrist and turn toward a top approach to the red mouse; keep left arm parked and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Align right gripper vertically over the mouse, descending only to a pregrasp height.
Correct mouse centering from wrist view, lower slowly and close around its sides; grasp retention remains to be checked.
Lift the closed mouse grasp and carry toward the mouse pad, checking visual retention before lowering.
Move mouse farther over pad and release near its surface. Mouse has rotated in the grasp, so verify its settled pose.
Mouse appears released near pad edge rather than retained. Reposition safely to its left for a gentle centering push.
Lower closed right fingers just left of the overturned mouse and start a slow lateral push onto the pad.
Continue the slow centering push, then open and lift clear to inspect the mouse on the pad.
Mouse is now visibly supported within the pad, though inverted. Move both wrists toward separate front-side keyboard pushing positions.
Bring closed fingertips toward two separated points behind the keyboard, rotating the left wrist to a downward approach without crossing arms.
Lower both closed fingertips to keyboard-edge height and approach its front edge slowly, watching for contact.
Push keyboard slowly forward and slightly right toward its frame. Figurine has tipped near the left edge and will need recovery.
Keyboard did not translate; fingertips were too high. Withdraw behind its edge, then lower for a true edge-level push.
Ease slightly above table contact and approach keyboard front edge at the corrected height; monitor displacement rather than tracking residual alone.
Keyboard has begun sliding. Continue a slow coordinated forward-right push while keeping each arm on its own side.
Keyboard is closer to its frame, but the clock obstructs further travel. Lift clear and approach the clock with the left arm; withdraw right arm.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller forward increments and a slightly lower left wrist, preserving joint continuity while approaching the clock.
Lower left fingers around the clock and close gently, while bringing the right arm toward its origin. Verify clock retention next.
Test clock retention with a small upward-left lift, avoiding further forward reach; finish returning the right arm to its origin.
Clock remained on the table after the test lift. Reopen and correct the approach farther forward and lower around its body.
Use a shallower clock approach with the wrist farther back to restore reach margin; small increments follow the continuity interruption.
Advance the angled left gripper around the clock body using wrist centering, then close; retention still needs a lift check.
Hold the clock grasp closed, then test retention with a small leftward lift that also improves reach margin.
Clock follows the wrist in RGB. Carry it up and left toward the drawer, maintaining a fully closed grasp and keeping the right arm parked.
Raise the retained clock above the drawer rim while moving over the left-side top surface; use small increments near the elevated posture.
Avoid further vertical folding after the guard interruption. Move laterally over the drawer with a slightly shallower wrist angle, keeping the clock closed in the grasp.
Advance the retained clock farther over the drawer top and lower gradually, keeping motion small near the folded posture.
Clock is over the drawer surface. Release without further forward reach, then retreat gently backward to avoid the IK limit and inspect settling.
The release executed but retreat was rejected. Use much smaller backward and slightly downward increments to move away from the folded IK boundary.
Elbow posture changed unexpectedly during retreat. Carefully reverse that short segment before selecting a safer withdrawal direction; keep clock released.
Withdraw from the released clock while flattening the wrist to lift fingertips clear and reduce the extreme elbow posture.
Prior withdrawal was rejected without motion. Try a smaller backward path with opposite wrist adjustment, monitoring continuity and clearance.
Clock remains on the drawer. Clear its front edge, then move above the fallen figurine and turn the jaws across its body for recovery.
Use smaller yaw and translation increments after the guard. Approach above the figurine with jaws turning perpendicular to its long axis.
Finish turning the left jaws across the fallen cactus stem and descend to a cautious pregrasp above its midpoint.
Lower around the cactus stem, which is centered between the left jaws, and close before attempting a lift.
Lift the closed cactus grasp clear of the keyboard and test whether the figurine follows before turning it upright.
Figurine follows the lift. Begin turning its long axis upright while moving the wrist left and toward the stand, keeping the grasp closed.
Complete the upright rotation and carry the closed figurine grasp over the small stand; keep enough height to inspect base alignment before lowering.
The figurine is nearly upright; avoid further wrist rotation near the continuity limit. Lower and center its base over the stand using small translations.
Downward motion met resistance and did not track. Base appears already near table height; slightly lift and shift toward the stand rather than forcing lower.
Release the upright figurine near the stand and withdraw toward the front, away from the drawer side that obstructs further alignment.
Figurine fell after release; its base was not supported. Clear the drawer and return to a top-down approach for a safer front-facing regrasp.
Align above the fallen figurine and turn the jaws across its stem, keeping the wrist clear before descending.
Lower the aligned jaws around the cactus stem at its new resting location, then close without moving it sideways.
Seat the jaws slightly lower on the stem, hold closed, and perform a short retention lift before reorientation.
Figurine is retained. Lift well clear and yaw it so the eventual upright placement can be approached from the front rather than beside the drawer.
Continue yawing the retained figurine over open space, aligning its stem toward the stand before the upright tilt.
Tilt the retained stem toward vertical with its pot below the grasp, keeping the wrist in front-left of the stand and clear of the drawer.
Finish the upright tilt and lower while advancing toward the stand. Keep the grasp closed until the pot is visibly supported, not just aligned in the image.
Avoid further rotation at the wrist continuity boundary. Lower the upright figurine toward the stand while making only a small centering correction; retain the grasp.
Correct the pot slightly left over the stand and lower in millimeter increments. Keep the figurine held until its base is supported.
Further centering is obstructed. Open fully without withdrawing, allowing the upright figurine to settle near the stand before checking support.
Figurine now stands after release but is right of the stand. Withdraw fully before a front-facing regrasp to center it without hitting the drawer.
Approach the upright stem from the front with open jaws, avoiding the drawer; prepare a small leftward correction onto the stand.
Center the front-facing jaws on the upright cactus using wrist and head views, then close before a small supported relocation.
Lift the upright figurine only slightly and shift left over the stand, retaining the front-facing grasp and avoiding the drawer.
The figurine did not follow the lateral test, indicating a missed grasp. Reopen, recenter on the stem, and advance slightly farther before closing.
Close fully around the centered upright stem, then test a small lift and leftward shift while watching whether the pot follows.
The pot followed this grasp. Finish the small leftward correction and return it to its supported height before opening over the stand.
Withdraw without disturbing the supported figurine, then bring both arms toward separated keyboard pushing positions to finish its frame alignment.
The rejected tilt would wrap the left wrist joint. First unwind it slightly while withdrawing, and continue the right arm's clear approach.
Turn both grippers toward separate keyboard-edge approaches, continuing a little left-wrist unwind to stay away from its joint wrap boundary.
Replan after the rejected branch change: unwind the left wrist around its current tool axis while withdrawing; advance only the right gripper toward the keyboard.
With left wrist unwound, turn it downward toward the keyboard's left-front edge. Lower the right fingers to pushing height without advancing yet.
Keep the left wrist short of its wrap limit and lower its angled fingertips to edge height. Ease the right fingers off table contact and approach the keyboard slowly.
Advance both closed fingertips into the keyboard edge, with slightly more left-side travel to square it toward the frame.
Right side moved more than the left. Lower the angled left fingertips to engage the edge and advance only the left side to square the keyboard.
Keyboard is moving and nearly square. Make a small forward-right adjustment, with a little extra left-side travel toward the frame.
Keyboard appears near the frame. Open and withdraw both arms into their separate workspaces to inspect alignment and begin returning home.
Keep the organized items undisturbed while unwinding the left wrist away from its joint boundary and returning both arms toward home.
Continue smooth left-wrist unwinding above its home position and settle the right arm at its origin, with both grippers open.
